title: Organization and licensing
summary: Regions, roles, divisions, named and concurrent licenses, packages, and fair use.

lessons.title: Place the organization in a core region
lessons.summary: You do not move an org between regions as a setting. You create it in a core region and live with that login host.
paras: The regions article is explicit: the organization is deployed in a core region chosen from its location, and users sign in on that region’s URL. Satellite regions never become that home. If a runbook says “point the org at the satellite closest to the agents,” it has mixed media design with org identity.

Genesys Cloud Voice is not available in every core region, and country coverage inside a region is restricted. The FedRAMP region’s voice article limits non-US country services. The European Sovereign region has its own boundary rules for where voice may be processed. Read those pages before you promise a number in a country.

cites.title: AWS regions for Genesys Cloud Voice

lessons.title: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions
lessons.summary: A role without a division grant does not open objects. An OAuth client inherits only a subset of its creator’s pairs.
paras: Divisions overview is the access model: you grant a role on a division, and the user sees objects in that division. Queues, users, and flows are configuration objects you place. Conversations and recordings are transactional and pick up division context as they move.

When you create a client-credentials OAuth client, you assign role and division pairs. The developer guide says those pairs are limited to a subset of what the creating user already has. A client cannot be used to escalate past its creator. It also cannot call /api/v2/users/me, because there is no user.

figure.caption: A role meets a division. The client cannot outgrow its creator.

lessons.title: Named licenses and the concurrent peak
lessons.summary: Concurrent billing charges the peak of simultaneous users, and it ignores peaks shorter than 30 minutes.
paras: The concurrent licensing article says Genesys charges the maximum number of simultaneous users in the billing period, after discarding peaks shorter than 30 minutes. Peaks do not have to be one continuous block. The charge uses the highest Genesys Cloud CX license those users held during the period. The calculation stays inside one organization. It does not combine orgs.

If you choose concurrent, the article says CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, and CX 4 users on that choice are licensed as concurrent. Named licensing is the other model: you assign a license to a person whether or not they are logged in. Fair use allocations also differ by named and concurrent user type, and the policy page is where those tables live.

figure.caption: A 20-minute spike does not set the concurrent bill. A 40-minute plateau does.

lessons.title: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose
lessons.summary: Match the package to the job. Do not buy CX 1 and then design a WFM project.
paras: Use the overview as the menu. Voice-only operations fit CX 1. Omnichannel plus quality fits CX 2. Scheduling, forecasting, and the transcription minutes that WEM expects fit CX 3. Agent Copilot and Journey Management, plus the published token counts, fit CX 4.

The fair use policy also names other commercial shapes, including Communicate, digital package variants, and EX, plus hourly user types. Those names exist on the policy. Their current allowances are rows in that table, not numbers this lab copies. Agent Copilot’s own article describes knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, forms, and written notes. That feature list is the copilot article, and the package that includes it is the overview.

lessons.title: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line
lessons.summary: Users live in the org. Queue membership is not the same thing as a division, and it has a hard cap.
paras: Create the person, place them in a division, and grant a role. Membership on a queue is a further step, capped at 5,000 members, and the queue itself sits in one division. A person can be a member of a queue only if your access model lets you see both.

Stations and phones come later, with Edge groups and WebRTC trunks. Do not block org design on hardware. Do decide which division owns the queue before agents are added, because moving it later changes who can administer it.

lessons.title: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
lessons.summary: Licenses include monthly allowances. Overage is priced on the policy page. Copying the numbers into a design doc freezes them wrong.
paras: The fair use policy describes consumption on top of the user license: BYOC Cloud minutes, data storage, basic routing and IVR, API requests, voice transcription, BYO SMS, workitems, and Journey Management events are among the families on that page. Allowances are monthly, they pool across users, and they do not roll over. Named, concurrent, and hourly user types are all in the policy’s language.

API calls made with a client-credentials integration count toward the API allowance. A lab that polls conversations every second is a bill, not a demo. Transcription minutes are a different meter from the user license, which is why CX 3 calls them out separately. When you estimate, open the policy and read the row. Do not reuse a figure from this paragraph.

fault.title: Polling bill
fault.symptom: API overage appears in the first month of a new dashboard.
fault.log: Job: GET conversations every second, all day.
fault.cause: That is on the order of millions of requests. The policy prices API requests.
fault.fix: Poll on an event or lengthen the interval, and read the allowance before you ship the job.

lessons.title: A first-week admin checklist
lessons.summary: Week one is region, divisions, roles, packages, one queue, and a published in-queue flow. Telephony can follow.
paras: Create or confirm the org in the right core region. Create the divisions you will actually administer. Grant roles in pairs. Assign packages that match the scope. Create one queue with a legal name, a division, a language if you need one, and fewer than 5,000 members. Publish the default in-queue call flow or the queue will be silent.

Then decide Genesys Cloud Voice versus BYOC, because emergency responsibility changes with that choice. Do not create a client-credentials OAuth client with All-division admin “just for now.” The subset rule exists so that temporary clients do not become the back door.
